text:
neha: heads up — noticed transient stalls and gRPC retransmits hitting model-serving pods on p5 clusters since 03:10 UTC. impact: tail latency spikes, a few failed inferences.

alex: saw the alert grafana panel. looks like drops on pod-to-pod streams, small packets. any correlation with autoscale?

neha: yes — most incidents around pod reschedule windows. also seen when node drains finish and pods land cross-rack.

jun: any packet captures? can we get raw tcpdump from affected pods and host veth/vxlan?

neha: uploaded a short pcap to /artifacts/pcap-1767812345.pcap. tcpdump on host showed a burst of retransmits and dup-acks for 64-256B packets.

olga: throwing some quick checks: `ip link show` on host, `bridge fdb show`, `ethtool -S` on mlx5. also check `dmesg` for offload errors.

neha: output snippets below — abridged:
```
# ip link show dev vxlan0
4: vxlan0: <BROADCAST,MULTICAST,UP,LOWER_UP> mtu 1450 qdisc noqueue state UNKNOWN mode DEFAULT group default qlen 1000
    link/ether aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff brd ff:ff:ff:ff:ff:ff
# bridge fdb show br0
00:11:22:33:44:55 dev vxlan0 self permanent
# dmesg | tail -n 5
[ 1024.123456] mlx5_core 0000:03:00.0 en: NETDEV WATCHDOG: enp3s0f0 (mlx5_core): transmit queue 0 timed out
[ 1024.123789] IPv4: martian source 10.10.0.1 from 10.10.0.2, dev vxlan0
```

maya: interesting — MTU shows 1450 on vxlan0. are hosts on jumbo or standard?

neha: hosts configured for 9000, but overlay endpoints ended up at 1450 because of a config push last week that set MTU by CNI to 1450.

alex: that mismatched MTU could cause fragmentation/encap issues, but we usually see PMTUD or larger drops. this is small-packet chatter. what about GSO/TSO/GRO offloads?

jun: can you run `ethtool -k` on enp3s0f0 and `ethtool -k vxlan0`? also output of `ss -tmi` for one of the affected connections.

neha: ethtool -k shows GSO/TSO on for host NIC; vxlan0 shows GSO off (kernel veth translation), GRO on. ss shows a lot of retransmits on port 50051 (model grpc).

net-ops-bot: incident-detection: detected 8 distinct retransmit spikes in cluster-p5-us-west-2 between 03:08-03:14 UTC. Nodes impacted: gpu-node-cc-12, gpu-node-cc-19, gpu-node-dd-07.

olga: another data point — `bridge fdb` had duplicate FDB entries during a reschedule, then they cleared. could be transient learning storm causing packets to be blackholed until FDB stabilizes.

alex: did we see any RDMA or mlx5 errors? dmesg showed NETDEV WATCHDOG on mlx5 — suspicious. could be CPU softirq saturation or doorbells delayed; that often shows up during heavy GPU memcpy/noise.

maya: also saw increased kworker CPU on those hosts around the same time.

jun: hypothesizing chain: pod reschedules -> bursts of small gRPC streams -> bridge learning churn + FDB flushes -> some packets forwarded to vxlan before fdb learned -> kernel drops? plus NIC offload weirdness (tso/gso) -> retransmits.

neha: repro attempt: triggered a rollout for a model (scale 100 -> 250) and watched similar small blips at scale boundary. CPU on host netstack spiked, and model clients saw ~50ms bursts then back to normal.

alex: quick mitigation options? 1) pin model-serving pods to same rack to avoid cross-rack vxlan paths during rollouts, 2) bump CNI MTU to 9000 and restart CNI on hosts (risky), 3) disable TSO/GSO on NICs or vxlan interface temporarily, 4) add a short delay to rollout to spread reschedules.

olga: we tested option 3 in a canary: `ip link set dev enp3s0f0 tso off gso off gro off` and `ip link set dev vxlan0 gro off` on a single host — retransmits dropped dramatically for the canary. CPU budget increased but latency stabilized.

neha: added a temporary automation to apply offload-disable on the three impacted nodes; clients report no more tail spikes in the last 20m.

net-ops-bot: action logged: created ticket INFRA-3219 to track root cause and rollback plan. assigned to neha + alex + olga.

maya: longer-term we should: - investigate mlx5 watchdog messages, - tune CNI to avoid MTU mismatch, - rate-limit reschedules during large rollouts, - add better bridge FDB event monitoring.

jun: also check kernel versions — some older kernels had vxlan GRO/GSO handling bugs with mlx5. what kernel are these hosts on?

neha: hosts running 5.15.83-1; will file a kernel matrix check.

alex: next steps for now: keep offload-disable on affected nodes, schedule a maintenance window to test MTU bump in staging, run a controlled mega-rollout with staged drifts, and confirm mlx5 firmware/driver updates.

olga: note — we'll need a rollback plan for offload-disable (it raises CPU and can affect throughput at peak). put a 4h expiry on the automation and page owners if CPU crosses threshold.

neha: done — automation set with 4h TTL and alert if host net CPU > 60%. I'll follow up with artifact pcap + ss output in the ticket. Thanks everyone :thanks: 

alex: added a doc stub in confluence — `Network/Intermittent-small-packet-blips` with initial findings.

maya: marking this thread resolved for now, keeping incident ticket open for RCA and follow-ups.

sre-bot: closed the alert channel. if any new spike, it will reopen the incident.
